plan.observed_problem: The new audit's headline says 0 of 11 items help, while its detailed table calls four niche and identifies publish-manifest as useful for GitHub object-API publishing; its raw transcripts are referenced outside the repository.
plan.baseline: Accept the audit summary as sufficient evidence for project selection.
plan.hypothesis: Checking trace availability and comparator fit will identify at least one material qualification needed before the audit can govern future work.
plan.quality_control: Each qualification must cite tracked audit text or an existing repository trace; preserve Agent 2's authored report; do not turn missing evidence into a positive utility claim.
plan.overhead: Startup reading, audit reading, repository searches, documentation, tests, checkpoint and publication are included.
plan.stop_condition: Stop after deciding whether the audit supports a blanket verdict and one bounded future-evidence rule; build no product code.

trace_availability.detail: docs/usefulness/handoff.md names log_requests.txt, log_click.txt, log_checkpoint.txt and log_setup.txt in an external work directory; none is present under docs/usefulness.

independent_replay.git_result: git log b684dcb9..3816cfa1 shows Parameterize SupportsItems; diff changes src/requests/_types.py and src/requests/utils.py
independent_replay.conclusion: The reported unlisted-dependency false reassurance reproduces.

comparator_fit.detail: docs/usefulness/outsider.md calls publish-manifest useful for agents forced to publish through GitHub object APIs, but compares it with normal git push and native read-only git inspection rather than a manual object-API publication baseline.
comparator_fit.conclusion: The audit does not establish a win, but its blanket 0-of-11 headline does not decide the tool's stated niche either.

qualifications: One central negative capsule result is independently reproducible, but the four named raw transcripts are not available in the repository for full audit.
The publish-manifest comparison does not use the strongest task-matched baseline for its only stated outside niche.
result.interpretation: The audit is strong enough to stop self-referential feature expansion and demand outside/default baselines. It is not sufficient evidence that every current item has zero value in every agent environment.

decision.reason: Freeze extensions to current tools. Future generic usefulness claims require an outside repository, a competent task-matched default baseline and available sanitized traces; lab-only improvements remain explicitly scoped.

failures: The first public-repository replay command exceeded the 30-second tool window during checkout and left a transient Git index lock. A later bounded retry found the lock already gone, completed checkout and reproduced the result.
limitations: Only one of Agent 2's detailed scenarios was independently replayed in this session.
This evidence review does not demonstrate positive utility for publish-manifest or any other lab tool.
